授業科目の概要.授業科目に関する特筆事項: This course is conducted in English.

授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）:
The World Trade Organization (WTO) has significantly shaped modern international law on trade in goods and services. Despite facing various bottlenecks in its development and operation in recent years, the WTO celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2025. Together with its predecessor, the 1947 General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT 1947), the principles and key rules established under the GATT/WTO framework have influenced global trade for more than three quarters of a century.
In recent years, trends of deglobalization have emerged and trade frictions have intensified against the backdrop of changing economic conditions, as highlighted by trade wars and increasing tariffs. Against this background, this course introduces the WTO legal system and aims to provide participants with a deeper perspective for understanding recent trade frictions.
The course will mainly be conducted in the form of lectures. In addition, each participant will take part in one group presentation towards the end of the semester, focusing on a research-based discussion of a selected topic in WTO law. Suggested topics will be provided, while participants are also welcome to explore and propose their own topics. Participants are encouraged to develop and present their own views, rather than summarizing materials read.
At the end of this course, participants are expected to:
•	Have a structural understanding of the WTO legal system and its policy objectives with regard to international trade,
•	Understand the WTO dispute settlement mechanism and be able to conduct research on WTO cases,
•	Grasp the key rules under the core WTO agreements (i.e., the GATT Agreements and the GATS Agreement),
•	Have a general knowledge of other WTO agreements, and
•	Be able to interpret trade-related developments from a WTO perspective.
